text: Hush… Don't stamp so. The wood doesn't like loud folk. It's frightened enough as it is.
Ah, the lamplighter. Oldrich said you'd come. Mind you, he said it twenty years ago. I decided you'd got lost.

choices.text: Why do you live here alone?
How do I find the beacon?

alone.text: When the beacons went out, people stopped coming to me for herbs. Why heal, they said, if it's dark anyway. I took offence and stopped going out. Foolish, isn't it? A grudge is a shade too — only your own, a homemade one. You almost feel sorry to chase it off.

text: The paths here lead in circles. Not because the wood is wicked — it's just tired and has forgotten where roads go.

But the fireflies remember. They fly to the beacon, even a dead one. Follow the ones that fly, not the ones that circle. And don't argue with the path: if it brought you back, you turned the wrong way — it didn't cheat you.

choices.text: And if I get lost anyway?

lost.text: Then stop, catch your breath and raise the lantern higher. Getting lost is no shame. Pretending to know the way when you don't — that is.

ask.text: Since you're going deeper — gather some glowcaps for me. Three of them. They glow right beside the paths, where the earth remembers light. They make a brew that gives people dreams. Good ones. No one in the Ford has dreamed of anything for a long time.

waiting.text: Looking for glowcaps? Three are needed. No rush — they won't run away. Mushrooms are the most patient folk in the wood.

alt.text: Wait… is that mint you have? It smells like Mara's mint, I know her thyme. Did she send anything? No? Well, never mind. Mint is a letter in itself. Look for glowcaps by the paths, three of them.

brought.text: Three glowcaps! Look how they shine — like little lanterns, only quiet. Thank you, lamplighter.

choices.text: Will you take the brew to the Ford?

dreams.text: Lia, for one. Mara once told me: the girl sleeps and sees nothing. Darkness outside is half the trouble. The trouble is when it's dark inside too.

brought2.text: I'll take it. Myself. It's time. Twenty years of sulking isn't patience, it's just stubbornness. Take some oil for the road — and my notebook. Everything I've understood about this wood is in it. Not much, but honest.

later.text: The brew is steeping. You can smell it across the whole glade. If the fireflies start circling again — go where they fly. They don't make mistakes.

text: Do you hear? A woodpecker! Knocking like at a door. I've waited so many years for someone to knock.
You know… I think I'll open it. And go to the Ford. Today. Not tomorrow.
And you — go east, to the Mire. There's a beacon on an islet, and only old Korney ferries people there. If he's still alive. He's more stubborn than me — so he's alive.
Moonwort. Four stalks, and all whole — you gathered them with care.
For Borta? I thought so. He burns himself every winter and every winter he says nothing.
Sit by the fire while I brew… There. Morning and evening. And tell him: keeping quiet about pain is not strength. Strength is walking to the one who can help.
